hook.text: Facebook gives you 80+ privacy settings. Most are designed to make you feel in control without being in control.

buildup.text: Platforms offer complex privacy dashboards that let you toggle options — but the defaults always favor sharing.

discovery.text: Studies show that fewer than 5% of users ever change their default privacy settings.

twist.text: Even when you restrict settings, platforms still collect data for their own use — just not publicly visible.

climax.text: Privacy settings give the illusion of control. Real control would mean less data collected in the first place.

punchline.text: Eighty settings. The illusion of control.

quiz.question: Why are social media privacy settings often criticized?
options: They create an illusion of control while defaults favor maximum sharing
They make platforms harder to use
They block all advertising by default
